subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group-chat isolation be solved by extending sender-scoped sessions/thread bindings, by automatic per-user group subagents with separate skills/config/memory, or by a plugin experiment first?
rationale: Current main has partial primitives, but the requested architecture changes durable agent lifecycle, security boundaries, per-user memory, and admin control; automation should not choose that product/security boundary.

options.title: Design Narrow Channel Isolation First
options.body: Use current groupSessionScope and session-binding architecture as the baseline, then add only the missing Feishu or SDK seams after resolving related threading and multi-bot identity issues.

options.title: Sponsor Per-User Group Subagents
options.body: Accept the proposed architecture and require a design for TTL, warm pools or cold starts, quotas, permissions, memory tiers, and migration or doctor behavior before implementation.

options.title: Prove As Plugin Experiment
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core lean by asking for an external Feishu plugin or ClawHub proof and promote only a missing generic SDK hook if current plugin APIs are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Design Narrow Channel Isolation First
recommendation.body: Use current groupSessionScope and session-binding architecture as the baseline, then add only the missing Feishu or SDK seams after resolving related threading and multi-bot identity issues.

likelyOwner.reason: Their verified adjacent Feishu ACP/session-binding history is closest to the subagent/thread-binding design decision this issue needs.
